_about: Claims registry seed v1 (D-8). Only the rows under 'Verified stats — safe to use' in li-lead-gen-tools/docs/research/stalled-pilot-evidence-brief.md (2026-11-03), with their sources. Nothing from the 'use with caution' or 'do not use' sections is here. `stat` is the brief's wording; `key_phrases` are short strings a claim may contain that identify the stat without a number.

claims.stat: 88% of orgs use AI in at least one function; only 39% report any EBIT impact, and most of those say under 5% of EBIT
claims.title: The state of AI in 2025

claims.stat: ~6% are "AI high performers" (5%+ of EBIT from AI and significant value)
claims.title: The state of AI in 2025

claims.stat: High performers are nearly 3x as likely to fundamentally redesign workflows
claims.title: The state of AI in 2025

claims.stat: Only 5% of companies are "future-built" and get AI value at scale; 60% get minimal or no material value; 35% are scaling with limited results
claims.title: The Widening AI Value Gap

claims.stat: 10-20-70: 10% of AI value from algorithms, 20% from data and tech, 70% from people and process
claims.title: 10-20-70 (restated on bcg.com, Jan 2026)

claims.stat: 42% of companies abandoned most AI initiatives in 2025, up from 17% in 2024; the average org scrapped 46% of proofs of concept before production
claims.publisher: S&P Global Market Intelligence / 451 Research, via CIO Dive
claims.title: AI project failure data (S&P Global)
key_phrases: abandoned most of their ai initiatives

claims.stat: At least 30% of GenAI projects abandoned after proof of concept by end of 2025, due to poor data quality, inadequate risk controls, escalating costs or unclear business value
claims.title: Gartner predicts 30% of generative AI projects will be abandoned after proof of concept by end of 2025
key_phrases: genai projects abandoned after proof of concept

claims.stat: Over 40% of agentic AI projects canceled by end of 2027 (costs, unclear value, inadequate risk controls); only ~130 of thousands of "agentic" vendors are real
claims.title: Over 40% of agentic AI projects will be scrapped by 2027 (Reuters via The Star)

claims.stat: Five root causes: problem misunderstood or miscommunicated; not enough data; tech chosen over the user's problem; weak infrastructure; problem too hard for AI
claims.title: Root Causes of Failure for AI Projects
key_phrases: root causes of failure for ai projects
